findings.title: Worldwide 12-month non-compete and ban on taking work from his AtliQ clients, imposed on an individual
findings.quote: For a period of twelve (12) months after termination or expiry of this Agreement, the Contractor shall not, anywhere in the world, directly or indirectly, provide any software or data services to any person
findings.explanation: After the contract ends Marcus could not provide software or data services to anyone, anywhere, in competition with AtliQ for twelve months (§8.1), and could not even accept work from any AtliQ client he served, which here means Lakeshore Grocers (§8.2). He is a US individual who would otherwise live off software and data work. Karandeep's note says a freelancer 'shouldn't get our paper and feel the way I felt reading Brightwater's', and he rejected a worldwide three-year reach on AtliQ itself at Al Noor. The signed freelancer paper, Rohan Iyer's, had only a six-month restriction on soliciting AtliQ clients. Whether Indian law and Pune courts can give a post-contract restriction effect over a Chicago resident is a question for counsel.

findings.title: AtliQ can end the contract on 24 hours' notice; Marcus must give 60 days
findings.quote: The Company may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving twenty-four (24) hours' written notice (including by email) to the Contractor.
findings.explanation: AtliQ may leave on 24 hours' notice by email; Marcus may leave only on 60 days' notice (§9.2). AtliQ may also end it immediately for 'unsatisfactory performance' (§9.3), a term the draft does not define and gives no chance to fix. On exit AtliQ pays only for approved hours (§9.4), and approval is at the project manager's discretion (F-04). The Rohan Iyer paper gave both sides 15 days and a 7-day fix period.

findings.title: Payment 60 days after a timesheet approval that AtliQ's manager gives 'at his discretion'
findings.quote: Payment shall be made within sixty (60) days after the date of timesheet approval.
findings.explanation: Two things stack: approval has no deadline and is at the project manager's discretion (§4.2), and the 60-day clock only starts at approval (§4.3). Karandeep's checklist is 30 days, 45 at most, and the signed Rohan Iyer paper pays within 30 days of invoice. Each month of Marcus's work (USD 58 x 40 x 4 = USD 9,280) could be unpaid for more than two months, with no cap on the approval delay. This is AtliQ's own paper, and the PixelCraft case shows the same 60-day clause was already corrected once for a small vendor.

findings.title: Pune company, Indian tax rules, Indian law and Pune courts for a US individual on a US-client project
findings.quote: The Company shall deduct tax at source (TDS) under Section 194J of the Income-tax Act, 1961 at the applicable rate and issue Form 16A.
findings.explanation: The draft is the India template: AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd as the Company, tax deducted under the Indian Income-tax Act (and at a higher rate if he has no PAN), optional GST, an Indian bank account in the schedule, Indian law and the courts at Pune, and Maharashtra stamp duty on Marcus. The project is for Lakeshore Grocers, whose draft MSA names AtliQ Inc as the vendor, and the entity sheet says AtliQ Inc serves US clients and Pvt Ltd serves clients outside the US. The tracker leaves the entity for C-040 blank. Whether the Pune entity should engage a Chicago freelancer for a US-client project, and how Indian tax mechanics apply to him, is a decision and a question for counsel. The draft's own checklist position (India law for Pvt Ltd) is met on its face.
